subject: Mathematics

source.subtopic: Introduce formal measuring: metre sticks, metre lengths of string; estimate and measure lengths in centimetres using a ruler

show.line: This is a ruler. The little steps are centimetres. The pencil reaches eight. It is eight centimetres long!

rounds.prompt: Read the ruler. How many centimetres long is the crayon?
Which one would you measure with a ruler?
rounds.praise: Yes! Small things fit on a ruler.

rounds.prompt: The paper clip starts at zero. Where does it end?
One hundred centimetres make one what? Say the word.
Which is longer than one metre?
rounds.praise: Yes! A door is taller than a metre stick.

rounds.prompt: Which ruler is read the right way, starting at zero?
Centimetres or metres? Pick the best unit for each.

hints: Line up the start with zero. Then read the number at the end.
Small things in centimetres. Big things in metres.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! I will measure the pencil.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: It starts at two and ends at ten. The pencil is ten centimetres!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! It did not start at zero. From two to ten is eight centimetres.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's start at zero together. Now the end says eight. Eight centimetres!

parent_line: Can read centimetres on a ruler and knows a metre is 100 centimetres.
